_comment: License allow-list for the CI license gate (scripts/license-gate.sh). A single detected SPDX id outside this list fails the pipeline. Additions to this list are deliberate, reviewed changes — never add copyleft (GPL/LGPL/AGPL/EPL/SSPL) without a maintainer decision.
_ignored_paths_comment: Path prefixes (relative to the staged scan tree) excluded from the gate. Use ONLY for documented false positives. Justifications: the license tooling itself (gate scripts + this policy file) necessarily names prohibited licenses; gen-third-party-notices.sh echoes license terminology; audit-license-provenance.py names licenses in its verdict maps; src/discover/discover.c contains a license-FILENAME classification list (LICENSE-MIT, LICENSE-APACHE, ...) for file discovery, which ScanCode reads as license references; package-release.sh and smoke-local.sh list the archive members 'hyp-integrations.json LICENSE ...' adjacently (the order the Windows one-executable runtime-set contract locks, mirrored by the smoke fixture), and ScanCode reads the '.json LICENSE' token adjacency as a reference to the SPDX 'JSON' license — first-party MIT build scripts, not vendored code. vendored/qwen3/NOTICE is a first-party attribution file for the Qwen3 static token-embedding table: it declares Apache-2.0, ships the canonical Apache-2.0 text beside it, and contains NO GPL text of any kind — verified by reading all 67 lines. ScanCode nonetheless resolves it to 'Apache-2.0 AND (Apache-2.0 AND (GPL-2.0-only OR Apache-2.0))', a compound dual-licence rule match on prose that discusses where the licence text came from. The near-identical vendored/qwen3-oldvocab/NOTICE does not trip it, which is itself evidence of a rule artefact rather than a real detection. NOTE: both qwen3 directories are dead weight — the static-table swap they exist for was MEASURED AND REJECTED (engine/hyponoia/runs/EMBED-SWAP), nothing in Makefile.hyp or src/ references them, and docs/THIRD_PARTY.md already says they are expected to be deleted. Deleting them is the better fix and is owed; this entry unblocks the first public release without doing surgery on the vendored tree in the same change.
